---

### Original (as written)

*In nomine Dei, amen. Ego Bartholomaeus Flandrensis, senex et infirmus corpore, sanus tamen mente, lego et relinquo Joanni nepoti meo domum meam cum omnibus bonis mobilibus et immobilibus. Item lego Catharinae, filiae quondam fratris mei Petri, viginti florenos. Actum in festo Sancti Galli, anno Domini MDCXLII.*

---

### Translation *(derivative — the original Latin governs)*

> "In the name of God, amen. I, Bartholomaeus Flandrensis, old and infirm in body, yet sound in mind, bequeath and leave to Joannes, my nephew [or grandson], my house together with all movable and immovable goods. Likewise I bequeath to Catharina, daughter of my late brother Petrus, twenty florins. Done on the feast of Saint Gall, in the year of the Lord 1642."

---

### Formulaic Latin Explained

| Latin phrase | Translation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| *In nomine Dei, amen* | In the name of God, amen | Standard testamentary opening formula across Western Europe |
| *senex et infirmus corpore* | old and infirm in body | Sets the scene; implies the will was made near death |
| *sanus tamen mente* | yet sound in mind | The legal capacity declaration — establishes mental competence |
| *lego et relinquo* | I bequeath and leave | Paired formula standard in Latin wills; both verbs mean essentially the same but together form a legally complete phrase |
| *bonis mobilibus et immobilibus* | movable and immovable goods | Standard property enumeration: *mobilia* = personal property (livestock, furnishings, money); *immobilia* = land and buildings |
| *Item lego* | Likewise I bequeath | *Item* is the standard enumerator in Latin wills ("also", "furthermore"); expect additional clauses in a longer will |
| *quondam* | late / formerly | Signals that Petrus is **deceased** at the time of writing — a key genealogical fact |
| *Actum* | Done / Executed | Dating formula marking when and where the act was carried out |
| *in festo Sancti Galli* | on the feast of Saint Gall | Saint Gall's feast day is **16 October** (1642-10-16) |
| *anno Domini MDCXLII* | in the year of the Lord 1642 | Roman numeral: M=1000, DC=600, XL=40, II=2 → **1642** |

---

### ⚠️ Critical Term: *nepos*

The Latin *nepos* is genuinely ambiguous and **must not be assumed**:

| Meaning | Latin expansion |
|---|---|
| **Nephew** (brother's/sister's son) | *nepos ex fratre/sorore* (explicit) |
| **Grandson** | *nepos ex filio/filia* (explicit) |

By 1642, Western European Latin wills increasingly used *nepos* for **nephew**, but both meanings remained in use. Since Bartholomaeus also mentions his **brother Petrus** in the same will, a *nepos* who is a nephew (son of another, unnamed sibling) is plausible — but so is a grandson. Other records (baptisms, earlier wills, parish registers) would be needed to resolve this.

---

### Genealogically Relevant Information

| Category | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Testator** | Bartholomaeus Flandrensis — *Flandrensis* is a toponym/surname meaning "of Flanders" or "the Fleming," suggesting origin in the Spanish Netherlands (modern Belgium/northern France) |
| **Testator's condition** | Old and infirm in body; sound in mind — will made near end of life |
| **Primary heir** | Joannes, described as *nepos* (nephew **or** grandson — ambiguous; see above); inherits the house and **all** movable and immovable goods |
| **Secondary heir** | Catharina, daughter of Bartholomaeus's **late** brother Petrus; receives 20 florins (a cash bequest, not real property) |
| **Relationship map** | Bartholomaeus ↔ Petrus: brothers · Petrus → Catharina: father-daughter · Petrus is deceased by 16 October 1642 |
| **Document date** | Feast of Saint Gall, 1642 = **16 October 1642 (1642-10-16)** — Gregorian calendar (Catholic Europe adopted 1582; no Old Style concern here) |
| **Currency** | *Viginti florenos* = 20 florins — a gold/silver coin widely used across early modern Europe; value varied by region and year |

---

### What to Watch For

- **Two lines of descent implied:** Joannes (primary heir) and Catharina (niece, secondary heir) may represent different branches — worth searching for Petrus's marriage and children separately.
- **Flandrensis as a locator:** If this is a place-of-origin surname, records in the Spanish Netherlands (Flanders, Brabant, Hainaut) may document Bartholomaeus's earlier life and family.
- **Petrus is confirmed deceased by 1642-10-16** (*quondam*) — useful for bounding his death date in searches.
- **The will does not name a wife or children of Bartholomaeus** — absence of evidence, but worth noting; he may have been a widower or childless, which would explain leaving the estate to a nephew/grandson and a niece.

### Kirchenbuch — German Parish Registers

A **Kirchenbuch** (literally *"church book"*; plural *Kirchenbücher*) is a **parish register** maintained by a Christian parish — primarily **Roman Catholic** and **Lutheran** — recording the three core vital events:

- 🔹 **Baptisms** *(Taufen)*
- 🔹 **Marriages** *(Trauungen)*
- 🔹 **Burials** *(Beerdigungen)*

- **Catholic parishes** began keeping them after the **Council of Trent (1563)**, with some registers reaching back to the **mid-1500s**.

| Repository | Records |
|---|---|
| The originating parish | Original volumes |
